b2-09-01.title: Communicative Challenge: If I Could Choose
b2-09-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks where you would live if you could choose anywhere. You imagine a place near a park in Budapest.
b2-09-01.prompt: Tell Carlos where you would live if you could choose, and what you would do there.
cues: Imagine where you would live if you could choose
Say one thing you would do there
b2-09-01.target: Si pudiera elegir, viviría cerca de un parque y saldría a caminar todos los días.
b2-09-01.english: If I could choose, I would live near a park and go for a walk every day.
b2-09-01.canDo: I can use si with the imperfect subjunctive and the conditional to imagine an unlikely situation.

b2-09-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Polite Booking
b2-09-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You are at the office and ring the front desk, because you need a meeting room for tomorrow morning.
b2-09-02.prompt: Politely ask the front desk for a meeting room for tomorrow.
cues: Say politely that you would like to book a room
Say which kind of room and for when
b2-09-02.target: Quisiera reservar una sala de reuniones para mañana por la mañana.
b2-09-02.english: I would like to book a meeting room for tomorrow morning.
b2-09-02.canDo: I can use quisiera, pudiera and debiera as softer forms of querría, podría and debería.

b2-09-03.title: Communicative Challenge: If You Would Be So Kind
b2-09-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are at a ticket office in Budapest and need the clerk to explain how to buy a ticket from the machine.
b2-09-03.prompt: Ask the clerk very politely to explain how to buy a ticket.
cues: Use a polite formula to ask for help
Say what you would be grateful for
b2-09-03.target: Si fuera tan amable de ayudarme, le agradecería que me explicara cómo comprar un boleto.
b2-09-03.english: If you would be so kind as to help me, I would be grateful if you explained how to buy a ticket.
b2-09-03.canDo: I can make a polite request with si fuera tan amable de and le agradecería que.

b2-09-04.title: Communicative Challenge: On One Condition
b2-09-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Your manager offers you a position in another office. You would accept it, but only on one condition: working from home some days.
b2-09-04.prompt: Tell your manager that you accept the position, and on what condition.
cues: Say that you accept the position
b2-09-04.target: Acepto el puesto a condición de que me permitan trabajar desde casa algunos días.
b2-09-04.english: I accept the position on condition that they allow me to work from home some days.
b2-09-04.canDo: I can set a condition with siempre que, con tal de que and a condición de que.

b2-09-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Unless It Rains
b2-09-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos invites you to a walk in a park in Budapest on Saturday. You want to go, but the weather could stop you.
b2-09-05.prompt: Tell Carlos that you will go on Saturday, and name the one thing that could stop you.
cues: Say that you will go on Saturday
b2-09-05.target: Iré al parque el sábado a no ser que llueva mucho.
b2-09-05.english: I will go to the park on Saturday unless it rains a lot.
b2-09-05.canDo: I can name the one exception that would change the outcome with a menos que, a no ser que and salvo que.

b2-09-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Different Job, On Terms
b2-09-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks whether you would change jobs. You would, but only if the new position left you free time.
b2-09-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what you would do and on what condition.
cues: Name the condition for the change
b2-09-consolidation.target: Si pudiera, cambiaría de trabajo, siempre que el nuevo puesto me dejara tiempo libre.
b2-09-consolidation.english: If I could, I would change jobs, provided that the new position left me free time.
b2-09-consolidation.canDo: I can imagine an unlikely present or future situation with si and the imperfect subjunctive.
